name: Garland
seo_title: Garland, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 7 Events
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Garland, TX: Christmas on the Square, Christmas at the Pullman, Snacks with Santa and two holiday plays, checked with each host.
lede: The story of Christmas in Garland is a downtown story: A Garland Christmas on the Square lights the tree on the town square, and the Garland Landmark Museum opens its 1901 Santa Fe depot for Christmas at the Pullman. The square exists because a fire in 1899 destroyed 28 of the town's 30 businesses and Garland rebuilt around it, a town that was itself created in 1887 between two rival railroad communities.
sections: A Garland Christmas on the Square

Downtown Garland packs its biggest holiday night into Friday, December 4, 2026. The square is open from 5 to 9 pm and the tree lights at 6:30 pm, according to the City of Garland and Visit Garland, with Santa on hand for visits. Kids can dance on an LED dance floor with DJ Pree, try interactive projector games, climb into a mega ball pit with slides and ride the North Pole Tubing Slide at La Grande's Feliz Navidad. Two family plays open the same night: The Best Christmas Pageant Ever at the Granville Arts Center, 300 N Fifth Street, and A Christmas Carol at the Plaza Theatre, 521 W State Street, both running through December 13 through Garland Cultural Arts.
The 1901 depot and the Pullman car

Garland's Christmas has a railroad heart. The Garland Landmark Museum sits in a vintage 1901 Santa Fe depot at 393 N Sixth Street, which the city dedicated as a museum in 1974 and which the Garland Landmark Society, founded in 1972, fills with exhibits and volunteers. Its Christmas at the Pullman day on Saturday, November 28, 2026, runs from 10 am to 4 pm with free admission, a gift market, photos with Santa and a historic Pullman railcar. The Handbook of Texas explains why the tracks matter here: rail lines bypassed Duck Creek in 1886, a new town grew between Duck Creek and Embree, and Garland was incorporated on April 21, 1891.
Light rail, a name nobody knew and a cowboy hat

Garland has light rail. DART opened its 4.5 mile Blue Line extension from Downtown Garland Station to Downtown Rowlett Station on December 3, 2012. The town's name has its own story: Congressman Joseph Abbott settled a name and incorporation dispute in 1887 by creating Garland between the two rival towns, and local legend holds that residents accepted the name of U.S. Attorney General Augustus H. Garland because nobody knew who he was. In 2013 the Texas legislature named Garland the Cowboy Hat Capital of Texas, thanks to makers such as Hatco.

faq: Garland was created in 1887 between two rival railroad communities. The Handbook of Texas says rail lines bypassed Duck Creek in 1886, a new town grew between Duck Creek and Embree, and Congressman Joseph Abbott settled the name and incorporation dispute. Garland was incorporated on April 21, 1891.
How did Garland get its name?

The town is named for U.S. Attorney General Augustus H. Garland. Local legend, as the Handbook of Texas tells it, says residents accepted the name in 1887 because nobody knew who he was. The compromise ended the dispute between the two rival towns that Garland was created to sit between.
What is the railroad history behind Garland's Christmas?

The Garland Landmark Museum sits in a vintage 1901 Santa Fe depot at 393 N Sixth Street. Its Christmas at the Pullman day on Saturday, November 28, 2026, runs from 10 am to 4 pm with a historic Pullman railcar, a gift market and photos with Santa. Admission is free.
What happens at Christmas for kids in Garland?

A Garland Christmas on the Square is Friday, December 4, 2026, from 5 to 9 pm, with the tree lighting at 6:30 pm, Santa, a mega ball pit with slides and the North Pole Tubing Slide. Garland Parks and Recreation also hosts free Snacks with Santa on December 8 at Fields Recreation Center.
Who organizes Christmas events in Garland?

The City of Garland and Visit Garland list A Garland Christmas on the Square, and Garland Cultural Arts runs the holiday plays at the Granville Arts Center and Plaza Theatre. Garland Parks and Recreation hosts Snacks with Santa, and the Garland Landmark Society runs Christmas at the Pullman.
Can families ride light rail to Garland?

Yes. DART opened its 4.5 mile Blue Line extension from Downtown Garland Station to Downtown Rowlett Station on December 3, 2012, so Garland has a light rail stop downtown. The tree lighting, the holiday plays and the depot museum are all in the downtown area.
